After thresholding $$\hat{y}$$ we compute a confusion matrix for our model's predictions. As a reminder, type $$0$$ and type $$1$$ refer to wine types. The confusion matrix contains the following counts:
• Actual type $$0$$, predicted type 0: $$57$$
• Actual type $$0$$, predicted type 1: unknown
• Actual type $$1$$, predicted type 0: unknown
• Actual type $$1$$, predicted type 1: $$62$$
For some reason, our confusion matrix is corrupted, and doesn't contain the information on the off-diagonals. However, we somehow know that our model's accuracy is $$ rac{119}{130}$$ and our model's precision is $$ rac{31}{32}.$$
